answer: A stake-bonded credential registry issues one anonymous credential per verified human via threshold cipher, with bonds locked at a public jetty contract; duplicate attestation roots are rejected and reward per credential is capped, so splitting stake across sybil agents adds full bond and verification cost but no extra payout. Attackers must forge the verifier or fund every accepted root; limitations include collusion, credential lending, and verifier capture. No single bond is treated as proof of a person; the harbor rule limits accepted roots per period.
